subject: Model suitability recap — prompt extraction & redaction intake
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Jennings <elliot.j@searchgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model suitability recap — prompt extraction & redaction intake

Hi Elliot,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the clarity on SearchGrid's intent and success metrics. Quick recap, recommendations, and asks below.

Recap
- Primary goal: Improve automated answer accuracy for customer support queries (target: 85% helpfulness on our internal rubric).
- Important constraints: explicit PII redaction, sub-1s median token latency for short queries, budget guidance: <$0.004 per 1k tokens.

Preliminary model recommendations
- rw-mix-13b (quantized q4f) — good balance of latency and quality for short answers.
- rw-45b-pt — higher-fidelity for long-context summarization and legal text.
- For rapid A/B: try rw-mix-13b vs rw-13b-q4 for throughput tests.
Benchmarks: https://redwood-internal/reports/model-benchmarks/rr-2028

What we need from you
1) Prompt corpus: a CSV with 200-500 representative user queries (column: id, prompt, expected_category, is_sensitive). Upload link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123
2) Edge-case list: 10–20 prioritized scenarios (examples below).
3) Confirmation of allowed redaction approach (we attached a short redaction checklist).

Edge-case examples (from today's call)
- Partial account numbers or masked identifiers
- Multi-turn conversation fragments quoting previous agents
- Code snippets or API keys embedded in user message
- Legal/regulatory text citations

Attachments: redaction-checklist.pdf

Next steps
- If you can share the sample CSV by next Tuesday (Apr 2), we will run a 100-sample eval and return a short report (latency, response similarity, safety hits) within 3 business days.
- If you'd prefer, Redwood can run the eval on Dedicated sandbox (we'll need an NDA for sample processing).

Proposed 30-min follow-up: https://calendly.com/redwood/jonas-searchgrid-30m

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Account Exec
Redwood Inference
From: Elliot Jennings <elliot.j@searchgrid.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: SearchGrid Legal <legal@searchgrid.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model suitability recap — prompt extraction & redaction intake

Jonas,

Thanks for the clear recap — this is helpful. I'm attaching a 250-row sample CSV (searchgrid_prompts_sample.csv) with a mix of real support queries (anonymized) and an "edge_cases" column where our support leads flagged the trickier inputs. A few notes pulled from the file so you have context:

- Example A: "I can't find my acct# 1234-****" (masked partial) — we want answers that avoid exposing anything even partially.
- Example B: multi-turn where user pastes a prior agent response and asks for clarification.
- Example C: code snippet that includes a dev API call; we need guidance on whether to strip or treat as text.

Question: For the preliminary eval, do you need us to pseudonymize names or can you accept the anonymized CSV as-is? Our legal team is copied for quick review.

Attachment: searchgrid_prompts_sample.csv (text/csv)

Elliot
Elliot Jennings
Head of Product
SearchGrid
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Jennings <elliot.j@searchgrid.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T20:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model suitability recap — prompt extraction & redaction intake

Elliot, Jonas —

Appreciate the sample. Quick technical notes from our side:

- On PII: for the preliminary eval we can accept the anonymized CSV. If SearchGrid prefers, we can run the eval in a Dedicated sandbox where we never persist raw inputs in the hosted plane; you'll get an audit log and we can bring in KMS for keys.
- Model recs (short): rw-mix-13b-q4f for low latency at scale; rw-45b-pt when you need legal/long-form accuracy.
- Eval run: recommended 200-sample run with buckets: short-helpful (<=50 tokens), long-summarize (>250 tokens), and safety/PII checks. We'll compute token-latency percentiles, response-similarity (BLEU/ROUGE-ish metric), and safety hit counts.

Bench harness: https://redwood-internal/reports/model-benchmarks/rr-2028

Jonas and I can run the preliminary 200-sample job if you grant the upload link and indicate whether you want the Dedicated sandbox. If you want us to do a deeper pass (redaction + regression tests), we'll propose a quick SOW afterwards.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Jennings <elliot.j@searchgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model suitability recap — prompt extraction & redaction intake

Elliot,

Perfect — thanks for the sample and the legal loop. Two quick confirmations and next steps:

1) Pseudonymization: acceptable to proceed with the anonymized CSV as-is for the initial run. If SearchGrid wants sandbox processing, reply with 'sandbox' and we will send a short NDA (DocuSign) and sandbox onboarding checklist.
2) We will schedule a 200-sample eval (Ben will lead). Tentative timeline: run on Apr 3, delivery Apr 6 (short report + recommendations).
3) Follow-up call: please pick a slot here and we'll use it to review results and discuss a scoped SOW for broader regression tests: https://calendly.com/redwood/jonas-searchgrid-30m

DocuSign (NDA): https://docusign.com/NTAdoc/SG-NDA-2028

Thanks again — looking forward to the results.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Account Exec
Redwood Inference
